Round 4, run 1 (../../curated-translation-candidates--world.md §5A: "Short excerpts, each translated from its own
language, set side by side … keyed to the unit being written now"). Translated by the run's coordinator. The Ugaritic
passages of the dossier (KTU 1.3 III 38–46, 1.5 I 1–8, 1.6 VI 44–53, 1.82, 1.83, 1.23:58–64) are translated in the
corpus's projects 1–2 and are referred to, not repeated, here.

Not done from the original, and why (world list §5A):

  • Ḫedammu (Hurro-Hittite, CTH 348): left in Round 4 (very fragmentary; no composite); the whole song was translated
    in Round 5 run 2 from the HPM edition (../../מיתוסים-חתיים-וחוריים/, key HE), and its sea-serpent passages joined
    the dossier at the Round 5 finalization (KEY HD, below).
  • The Deir ʿAllā bird list: no open edition (Hoftijzer & van der Kooij 1976 ©; DEAPS has no record yet).
  • Anaximander's first humans inside fish: only indirect testimonia (Censorinus in Latin, ps.-Plutarch in Greek); a
    candidate for a later "Greek beginnings" dossier.
  • The Avestan Aži Dahāka, Gandarəβa: Young Avestan, high risk; with the Vedic/Avestan project.
  • The Shanhaijing's birds and fish: ctext.org forbids scraping; zh.wikisource would serve – a later addition.
  • The Kumulipo's births; the Māori Ika-tere: the 1889 / 1854 texts are public domain but no clean digital text was
    reachable today (Ulukau and NZETC block scripts).
  • The Inuit Sea Woman: no text in the original language (only Rasmussen's and Boas's English and Danish).
  • The Ngaju Dayak hornbill and water-snake: Schärer's material is German with Ngaju phrases (CC BY-NC); no tools.
  • Palenque Temple XIX: Classic Maya hieroglyphic; not readable with control here.
  • The Russian Dove Book (the earth on a whale): a 17th–19th-century reception of Gen 1–2 rather than an old tradition;
    ru.wikisource answered 429 to scripts today.

Added later: the Apophis spells; the Westcar crocodile (Egyptian), first left to the Egyptian run: done Round 4
run 3 sub 2 (2026-10-24, KEYs WC and AP). The ranges: WC – the crocodile scene only (the making 2,21–2,23, the orders to
the steward 3,1–3,5, the throw, growth and seizure 3,11–3,16, the scene before the king 3,21–4,7: 27 AED lines, two over
the brief's 25, to keep 2,21 with the loanword hbnj הָבְנִים and the summoning 3,21); the adultery scenes 3,6–3,10
and the frame are summarized in notes. AP – one whole short spell-book (26,11-12–26,20) with the end of the spell before
it (26,8–26,11: "the lake of Nun") and the drawing rubric of the Names (32,43–32,45, 32,50: the serpent and the
crocodile-faced figure). The creation account that follows in the same papyrus (26,21 ff., "the book of knowing the
becomings of Re": Khepri, "when I came into being, being came into being") is not in the dossier – a pointer only
(AP 26,20, note); it belongs to the Egyptian corpus's creation project.

Method

  • One file per excerpt, annotated-<KEY>.rtl.md, in the corpus format (guidelines §7.2): the base line (@ +
    python3 -I -B dossier_tools.py fill), one Hebrew line, פירוק (from the source's own lemmatization where it has one:
    AED, VedaWeb, TLHdig), תרגומים (formed after the reading; AED's German only after drafting: data MK --tr), הקבלה,
    הערות. translation.rtl.md is built from translation--head.rtl.md + translation--intro-<KEY>.rtl.md + the >
    lines (dossier_tools.py build), and verified.
  • Renderings: ../renderings.md §11 (the comparison word נָחָשׁ; the never-words; names).
  • What the dossier can show (world list §5A): that Gen 1:21's created תַּנִּינִם stand alone against a world where the
    sea monster is a rival (Ugarit, Hatti, India, the North), a parent (Hesiod's Keto, the Egyptian waters' greed), or a
    slain body (Japan). The parallels are typological (no contact) except for Ugarit, Egypt and Hatti (contact cultures),
    and the Greek of the LXX (the translators' own vocabulary).
    • Egypt (WC, AP): the water monster as a made thing and as an uncreated enemy. In pWestcar a lector priest
      (ḥry-tp, the Hebrew חַרְטֹם) makes a wax crocodile that, thrown into the water, "becomes a crocodile" (ḫpr m =
      וַיְהִי לְ־) – the miracle of Ex 7:9–12, where Aaron's staff and the חַרְטֻמִּים' staffs "become תַּנִּינִם"; in the
      Apophis book the serpent of the primeval water is cursed with childlessness ("you shall not conceive, none shall be
      born to you"), burned daily in wax and drawn as a serpent and as a crocodile-faced figure – the exact reverse of Gen
      1:21–22, where the great תַּנִּינִם are created and blessed "be fruitful and multiply". Ezek 29:3 and 32:2 turn the
      Egyptian image round: Pharaoh, Apophis's foe in the papyrus, is himself "the great תַּנִּים".
  • Egyptian words follow ../../חכמה-ובריאה-במצרים/renderings.md (§3 names, §4 key terms, §10.1–10.12; checked with
    egypt_tools.py lex): msḥ תִּמְסָח (never תַּנִּין), ḥf / ḥfꜣw נָחָשׁ, Rꜥ רַא ★, ḥry-tp חַרְטֹם [cognate],
    ḫꜣꜥ הֵטִיל, šꜣs שׁוּט, jṯi̯ תָּפַס, ḥtp נָח, sḏ.t שַׁלְהֶבֶת, ḫ.t אֵשׁ, sḫr הִכְרִיעַ, mḏꜣ.t מְגִלָּה (סֵפֶר =
    šfd). New in the dossier (proposed to the Egyptian corpus, see the report): mnḥ שַׁעֲוָה, š אֲגַם, ḏꜣ.t עֹמֶק, ḥry-pr
    סוֹכֵן הַבַּיִת, nḥꜣ מְסֻכָּן (as AM 4.8), nsr.t לַהַט (the goddess נֶסֶרֶת), wꜣwꜣ גַּחֶלֶת, dm/tm כָּלָה, šp
    "perish" אָבַד / "be blind" סוּמָא, sḥtm הִשְׁמִיד, ḥtm הִכְחִיד, sswn רִסֵּק, qꜣjs כָּפַת, snḥ אָסַר, hꜣrp
    שָׁקַע (as AM 10.1), sḫd צָלַל, ṯs.t פַּסְלוֹן־קְלָלָה, sb-n-sḏ.t / sb-n-ḫ.t קָרְבַּן־שַׁלְהֶבֶת / קָרְבַּן־אֵשׁ.
    dossier_tools.py verify gates the loanwords and key words of WC/AP by their source word (LICENSED: תמסח – msḥ,
    חרטום – ḥry-tp, הבנים – hbnj, שעווה – mnḥ, נחש – ḥf/ḥfꜣw, פרעה – pr-ꜥꜣ) and traps an unvocalized רא.

Ḫedammu (HD; the Round 5 finalization, 2026-11-02)

  • Copied, not re-translated. The 60 lines are the myth corpus's own (../../מיתוסים-חתיים-וחוריים/1-אילויאנקה-וחדמו/annotated-HE.rtl.md,
    translated and reviewed in Round 5 run 2): dossier_tools.py reads the base through hittite_tools.py (rows("HE"):
    the same HPM clauses and TLHdig glosses, the labels <fragment>:<clause>), and hittite_tools.py verify HE checks that
    every HD entry's transliteration and > line equal HE's, byte for byte (as verify IL checks IL 8–17 against this
    dossier's IL). A revision is made in both files at once, or recorded in the myth renderings §H8 (| HE | … |) for the
    lead. The פירוק and תרגומים bullets are HE's; the הקבלה and הערות were rewritten for the dossier (Gen 1:20–22 and the
    other excerpts' serpents); the corpus's references to its own tables were re-pointed.
  • Selection (60 lines, the brief's upper bound): the four passages that bear on Gen 1:21 – the serpent's parents
    (Kumarbi and the Sea's daughter, 6:13–19), his birth in the Sea's house (21:12–16; the reading "birth" is HPM's and
    uncertain), his rearing and appetite (2:5–22), and Ištar's seduction at the sea with his cosmic size and the floods
    (4:10–39). Left out: fragment 1 (the famine, Ea's speech – Gen 6–8 rather than 1:21), fragment 8 (Ḫedammu sees Ištar
    again: the same scene as 4:23, more broken). The order is the story's (HPM numbers the fragments otherwise; their order
    is uncertain beyond fragment 1).
  • No נָחָשׁ in the lines: the Hittite writes the name with the determinative MUŠ "snake" ({MUŠ}ḫedammu), which is
    not translated (as Akkadian determinatives); the dossier's comparison word stays for the generic word, and the intro and
    notes call him "נחש הים". No dossier never-word (§11) occurs in the 60 lines; no gate was bent.
  • Key findings. (1) The sea monster has parents: a god and the Sea's daughter, a bride a DANNA wide (6:16–18) –
    against Gen 1:21, where the תַּנִּינִם are created, and close to Hesiod's Keto (TH 238), the Sea's daughter and mother of
    monsters. (2) He is begotten as a weapon in the war for kingship in heaven, not blessed to be fruitful (21:14 ↔ Gen
    1:22). (3) His appetite is the measure of his monstrosity: cattle and horses by the thousand, kids and lambs "without
    number" (2:14 ↔ Ps 104:25, where it is the sea's creatures that are without number), and the river's fish (2:19) – in Gen
    1:21–22 the תַּנִּינִם and the fish are created and blessed together, and Gen 1:30 gives all living things plants to eat.
    (4) His size is counted in cities (4:27–29 ↔ the "great" תַּנִּינִם; the Norse world serpent HY 22.7–8). (5) The
    drink that overcomes the serpent is shared with Illuyanka (IL i14–18) and Japan (KJ 9–10); the naked goddess
    who seduces the serpent (4:23) reverses Gen 3:1, where the serpent persuades the woman. (6) The serpent pours floods
    on the land and comes down "from the throne, from the sea" (4:38–39): the sea as a kingdom whose waters break their
    bounds, against Job 38:11 and Isa 27:1's הַתַּנִּין אֲשֶׁר בַּיָּם.

  • 2026-10-24 (Round 4 run 4 sub 1, the Hesiod corpus): the TH excerpt aligned with the full Theogony
    (../../הסיודוס/1-תולדות-האלים/annotated-TH.rtl.md, drafted and reviewed in three passes): all 23 > lines now carry
    the corpus's Hebrew for the same lines, so that the dossier and the corpus never give one Greek line two Hebrews.
    Reasons (../../הסיודוס/renderings.md §3.2, §5, §11, §12.2): Gaia is a speaking name translated אֶרֶץ (238, 821;
    West's and Most's "Earth"); γείνομαι הוֹלִיד (334); γένος גֶּזַע (336, not דור: γενεή has דּוֹר, the LXX's word of
    Gen 6:9); ζάθεος מְקֻדָּשׁ (300; ἱερός keeps קָדוֹשׁ); φρένες לֵבָב (239); אַפְרוֹדִיטָה (822); ἀμήχανος שֶׁאֵין כְּנֶגְדּוֹ תּוּשִׁיָּה (295); ἀγήνωρ אַמִּיץ (237: עַז־הָרוּחַ hits the corpus's רוּחַ gate, reserved for the winds);
    θεῖος / θεσπέσιος אֱלוֹהִי (297, 827); ὠμηστής אוֹכֵל־נָא (300); ἐρεμνός כֵּהֶה (334), δνοφερός קוֹדֵר (826); the
    corpus's epithets (מְעֻגֶּלֶת־הָעֵינַיִם 298) and 823 (a corrupt line, rendered closer to the Greek). Kept as the
    dossier's own: the vocalization of names at their first occurrence in this file, and the full stop of the excerpt's last
    line (828; the corpus line ends ;). The glosses of the פירוק and the notes that named the old Hebrew were updated
    (238, 239, 295, 300, 334, 336, the head). dossier_tools.py verify --strict 0 problems (no dossier gate blocked a
    corpus rendering), build done, check_bible_quotes 0.

  • 2026-11-02 (the Round 5 finalization): IL – the four revisions recorded by the myth corpus (its renderings §H8)
    applied: i12 ואל הסערה – את כל האלים → וְאֵל הַסְּעָרָה – אֶת כָּל הָאֵלִים (the Hittite trap: unvocalized "and to" /
    "these"); i15 והכינה הכול בשפע: → וערכה הכול לָרֹב: (ḫandai- עָרַךְ; mekki לָרֹב, שֶׁפַע being iyatar's, i18);
    i16–17 כלי … כלי … כלי – ובכלים → דוד … דוד … דוד – ובדודים ({DUG}palḫi- דּוּד); i19 ואִינָרָה [… ל]זִיגָּרָתָּה →
    ואִינָרָה [ל]זִיגָּרָתָּה (the gap holds only the preposition); the פירוק glosses and notes updated. HD (Ḫedammu)
    added, 60 lines (section above); build, verify --strict 0, hittite_tools.py verify HE --strict / verify IL --strict identical, check_bible_quotes 0.

RV 1.32 aligned with the full hymn (Round 5 run 1, 2026-10-30)

The whole of RV 1.32 is now translated in ../../הוודה-והאווסטה/2-אינדרה-והנחש/annotated-RV1.32.rtl.md; its 24 pādas
that are in this dossier carry the same Hebrew (checked by vedic_tools.py verify RV1.32). Two revisions were made in
both files: 5a vyàṃsa חסר־הכתפיים → פרוש־הכתפיים (ví "apart" + áṃsa: the cobra spreading its hood – Jamison,
after Hock; "shoulderless" would need a-), and 5d pr̥thivī́ לאדמה → לארץ (the Vedic corpus: pr̥thivī́ אֶרֶץ,
bhū́mi אֲדָמָה).
